newsitem.title: CHINA: Number of surplus rural workers in China tops 130 mln.
newsitem.headline: Number of surplus rural workers in China tops 130 mln.

text.p: China has 130 million surplus workers in its rural areas, and the number was expected to increase by the year 2000, the Legal Daily said on Thursday.

By the end of the century, the total number of new people in the rural workforce coupled with the surplus workers would swell to more than 210 million, while the number of new jobs was expected to be only 70 million, the newspaper said.

Only 200 million of China's 450 million rural workers were actually needed for farming and 126 million were employed by rural industries, leaving 124 million surplus rural labourers, a report said last year.

Finding jobs for surplus workers was hampered by a shortage of arable land, the unbalanced regional breakdown of surplus workers, and large numbers of urban workers laid-off from ailing state firms, it said.
By 1995, it was estimated that about 80 million rural labourers had moved to urban areas in search of work.

China's total labour force would swell in the next 30 years, peaking at 870 million by the year 2016, the Xinhua news agency said. The working-age population would remain above 800 million between 2003 and 2032.
The next three decades would see increased pressure from unemployment, it said without elaborating.
China's unemployment rate was expected to grow to 3.0-3.5 percent in 1997, an official newspaper said this week. The urban jobless rate was 2.98 percent at the end of last September.

China has not announced a jobless rate for 1996 and is usually reluctant to reveal the figure, but officials have said the government wants to curb the level at 3.2 percent in 1996. Urban unemployment was 2.9 percent in 1995.
China's total labour force was expected to reach 743 million in 1997, including rural areas, while total demand for labour was projected at 646 million, the newspaper said.
